title: Mission Kit catalogue entry frontmatter v1alpha1
description: Frontmatter contract for every ID-prefixed Mission Kit entry, whatever its category; the categories are the category enum below. Every property either changes how an agent acts on the entry or addresses the entry. Archival bookkeeping is excluded by construction: additionalProperties is false, so a reintroduced added, provenance, source-tele or retrieved field fails validation rather than accumulating unread.

id.description: Stable address. An entry that cannot be cited cannot be referenced from another entry or from an agent's context.

category.description: The set that governs this entry. Selects the directory that owns it and the ID prefix it must carry, and is the member-side declaration of set membership described by E3. The governing charter is resolvable from it without a lookup: it is the entry whose id is that set's prefix followed by zero, at <directory>/README.md. A member states what it is; its charter states what the population owes itself, and this field is the only link between the two.

title.description: Human-readable name, reproduced verbatim in INDEX.md.

status.description: Whether this entry is in force, and if not, why not. This field answers that question and no other: a requirement's progress and a work-type's generatability are separate concerns with their own fields, because conflating them is how five disagreeing vocabularies arose. active: in force, apply it. draft: not yet in force, do not apply. superseded: replaced, follow the entry whose supersedes names this one. retired: no longer in force, the ID is kept so citations resolve.

generatable.description: Whether the substrate can generate this work-type from the axes, or it must be authored by hand. A capability of the type, not a lifecycle state.

hydrate-when.description: The condition under which to open this entry, stated so an agent can evaluate it against what it is doing now. A topic never fires; see S14. Required: an entry nothing routes to has the same value as no entry.

enforced-by.description: The tool that holds this rule, relative to the repository root. Declaring it makes the pairing checkable: a rule claiming an enforcer that does not exist is a broken promise, and an enforcer with no rule is orphaned.

supersedes.description: Entries this one replaces. Following a superseded entry is an error, and only this field says so.

related.description: Adjacent entries worth hydrating alongside this one. Routing, not provenance.

applies-to.description: The traits a system must have at least one of for this axiom to bind it, or 'any-system' to bind every system. Each value other than 'any-system' is a trait declared in traits/, so a misspelled or undefined tag is refused rather than silently binding nothing. Values are alternatives, never a conjunction.

source.description: Upstream origin, permitted only where the entry is third-party content carrying a licence obligation.

composing.description: Whether the role composes into an arc symmetrically. Director is authority-only and does not.

sovereignty.description: Whether a component is owned here or referenced from outside. 'internal' is a sovereign unit under our own authority, so a fit gap is pressure that routes upstream and resolves by adjusting or fracturing the component itself. 'external' is a unit we do not control, so a fit gap has no upstream and must be adapted at our boundary, replaced, or absorbed.

internalisation-trigger.description: The observable condition under which an external component is replaced by a sovereign internal one. Required on every external entry so a dependency we do not own carries its exit condition, rather than becoming permanent by default.

trace.description: For a rule: the observable trace a check could test - what in the record shows the rule was kept or broken. A rule earns its layer by leaving one; a practice leaves none. Naming a tool that checks it is enforced-by's job, and is optional.

members.description: For a set spanning layers: the entries it gathers. The set's territory gives membership its meaning, so the set declares it, not the member. Each must exist and be active, which the index generator checks.
